title: Building Interactive UIs in VS Code with MCP Apps — Marlene Mhangami & Liam Hampton, GitHub
talk_summary: The talk explains MCP Apps: MCP servers return tool results plus a UI resource reference, and the host renders the HTML in a sandboxed iframe that can call back to the server. A demo wraps Go pprof profiling in an MCP server and renders an interactive flame graph inside VS Code chat.

takeaways.what_they_do: The host fetches server-returned HTML and renders it in a sandboxed iframe so the app cannot touch host settings or external APIs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the host is going to render the app inside a sandboxed iframe

takeaways.technique: UI resource reference plus server callback
takeaways.what_they_do: A tool result includes a UI resource reference; the host renders it, and the app can call back to the server for fresh data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: return the tool results with a UI a resource reference

takeaways.what_they_do: The MCP app skill defines whether only the model, only the app, or both can invoke a tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whether it's just the model that can call the application, whether it's the model and the app, or whether it's just the app

takeaways.what_they_do: They use a reusable skill/README with handlers, tool visibility, and code examples so Copilot CLI or Claude can generate MCP apps consistently.
takeaways.evidence_quote: tell Copilot CLI or Claude or whatever AI tooling that you're using how to run this

takeaways.technique: Wrap profiler as MCP server with structured output
takeaways.what_they_do: An MCP server bundles and runs a Go program, profiles it with pprof, and returns data that a React flame graph renders in the chat iframe.
takeaways.evidence_quote: MCP is going to bundle up my Go program, run it, profile it, and spit out some data

takeaways.what_they_do: They recommend using the VS Code/GitHub server list rather than random internet MCP servers because malicious servers are a risk.
takeaways.evidence_quote: sometimes you can have some security issues if you just go on the internet and pick a random server
